chapter: Army cornet and Bix's Bach horn
title: Bix buys him a Bach cornet
summary: In Chicago in 1928 Bix lets him try a new Bach cornet and pays $145 toward one for him at Dixie Music House.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Now the other horn you were talking about it's a Bach cornet and Bix Beiderbecke gave me this horn. He bought it for me actually. He was in Chicago with the Paul Whiteman Orchestra there in 1928 this was. And he came in with Paul Whiteman
and Bing Crosby and the Rhythm Boys. Jimmy Dorsey, Tommy Dorsey and we used to jam inbetween their shows over at a place called 'The Three Deuces' 222....
That used to be a famous club.

Yes, 'The Three Deuces', 222 North State Street. It was just half a block down over north of Lake Street. And Bix came in one day and when I was around he'd always say he wanted to play piano because he played piano too. So after he played a while on the cornet there he says to me listen kid he said, play my cornet, I've got a new horn he says, it's terrific. It just came out, it's a Bach coronet.

And he says, what do you think of it? So, he says I want to play piano anyway, Bix did. So he got over to the piano while I took his horn and I had my mouthpiece and put it in there and I blew the cornet and it's a beautiful horn. A Bach coronet, it was new in those days. I loved it. And he asked me how, after the session was over asked me how.... I said it's beautiful horn. He said, why don't you get one. I said, I haven't got any money, I'm not working you know. (LAUGHTER).
He said, well you meet me after the next show and we'll go over to the Dixie Music House over here

and we'll get one. I said, I have no money. He said, don't worry about it. This is the kind of a guy he was you know. Anyhow, kid he used to call me, kid all the time. So we went over to Dixie Music House and a new horn cost $175 I think it was. Pick one out, there were four of them. I blew them and said, this is the one, this is the good one.

Of course I knew the people there and he knew them. They knew him. So all he had was about $145 on him. He just pulled $145 out of his pocket and gave it to the man. And he said you can pay the rest of it, let the kid pay it off at five dollars a month, okay? He said sure, the guy said sure. (LAUGHTER).
Oh, he owed him thirty dollars yes.

So, yes, but he paid that up and bought it for me. And not only that but he took it with him on the road. He said, I'll break it in for you to get it right. He wanted to break the valves in right you know, push them down the same way.
And so he took the horn with him to St. Louis and came back about ten days later I think he did and gave me the horn.
